elements.description: A single-choice dropdown: a secondary-button trigger that opens a listbox of options.

properties.name: value
properties.description: The chosen option's value – unset or unknown shows the placeholder

properties.name: label
properties.description: The control's accessible name; shown above the trigger with `label-visible`

properties.name: labelVisible
properties.description: Show `label` above the trigger instead of only to screen readers

properties.name: labelPlacement
properties.description: Where the visible label sits, with `label-visible` only: "top", above the trigger (default), or "start", before it on the same line in the caption style. Without `label-visible` it changes nothing

properties.name: placeholder
properties.description: What the trigger says while no option is chosen

properties.name: align
properties.description: Which edge of the trigger the list lines up with

properties.name: disabled
properties.description: Turns the control off; the hidden form input is disabled too

properties.name: name
properties.description: Submits the chosen value with a native form, through a hidden input

properties.name: look
properties.description: Visual style: "standard" or "clean"; unset follows <tc-look-provider>, else "standard"

events.name: tc-value-change
events.description: An option was picked (`{ value: string }`: SelectValueChange); cancelable – prevent it to keep `value` (controlled use)

events.name: tc-open-change
events.description: The list opens or closes (`{ open: boolean }`: SelectOpenChange); cancelable

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's value (controlled when defined)

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value chosen at first when uncontrolled – none (the placeholder) by default

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the value of the option that was picked

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state of the list

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the list starts open when uncontrolled

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the list opens or closes

changelog: **Select:** `tc-select` (`@adamstavely/trenchcoat/select`, React `Select`, Angular `Select` from `@adamstavely/trenchcoat/angular/select`), a plain single-choice dropdown for a page or card header, or a form. - The trigger is a secondary button (the `--tc-action-secondary-*` and `--tc-control-*-md` tokens, so it lines up with the buttons beside it) showing the chosen option's label, or `placeholder` (“Choose…”) while `value` is unset or unknown, and a chevron. The list under it is the menu pattern: a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected`, a check on the chosen one and an optional `description` line; `disabled` options show but can't be picked. - `options: SelectOption[]` (`{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`), `value`, `label` (the accessible name – shown above the trigger with `label-visible`, else read by screen readers only), `placeholder`, `open`, `align="start" | "end"`, `disabled`, `name` (a hidden input for native forms) and `look`. - `tc-value-change` (`{ value }`) and `tc-open-change` (`{ open }`) are cancelable: prevented, `value` or `open` stays (controlled use). Angular gets a value accessor for `ngModel` and reactive forms. - ↓ / ↑ on the trigger open the list; in it the arrows, Home and End move past disabled options, Enter or Space picks, letters jump to the next option starting with them, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger, Tab or a click outside closes. Near the edge of the screen the list slides in to stay whole. Option ids come from their position, never from their values.

features.name: light-dark()
features.why: Every colour token is a light / dark pair; without it no colour token resolves.

features.name: color-mix()
features.why: Tints and washes mixed from the tokens.

features.name: inert
features.why: Closed and leaving parts are out of the tab order and hidden from screen readers.

features.name: :is() and :where()
features.why: Every rule is keyed on :where() so the page can override it.

features.name: adoptedStyleSheets
features.without: Each element type's CSS goes into one <style> element in <head> instead – it looks and works the same.

features.name: forced-colors media query
features.without: In a forced-colours mode the browser's own adjustments apply, without the components' fixes.

features.name: overscroll-behavior: contain
features.without: Scrolling past the end of a list carries on scrolling the page.
